exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 27–36, mark each statement True or False (T/F). Justify each answer.

problem.paragraph: (T/F) A homogeneous equation is always consistent.
(T/F) If $$\mathbf{x}$$ is a nontrivial solution of $$A\mathbf{x} = 0$$ , then every entry in $$\mathbf{x}$$ is nonzero.
(T/F) The equation $$A\mathbf{x} = 0$$ gives an explicit description of its solution set.

(T/F) The equation $$\mathbf{x} = x_{2}\mathbf{u} + x_{3}\mathbf{v}$$ , with $$x_{2}$$ and $$x_{3}$$ free (and neither $$\mathbf{u}$$ nor $$\mathbf{v}$$ a multiple of the other), describes a plane through the origin.
(T/F) The homogeneous equation $$A\mathbf{x} = 0$$ has the trivial solution if and only if the equation has at least one free variable.
(T/F) The equation $$A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$$ is homogeneous if the zero vector is a solution.
(T/F) The equation $$\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{p} + t\mathbf{v}$$ describes a line through $$\mathbf{v}$$ parallel to $$\mathbf{p}$$ .
(T/F) The effect of adding $$\mathbf{p}$$ to a vector is to move the vector in a direction parallel to $$\mathbf{p}$$ .

(T/F) The solution set of $$A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$$ is the set of all vectors of the form $$\mathbf{w} = \mathbf{p} + \mathbf{v}_{h}$$ , where $$\mathbf{v}_{h}$$ is any solution of the equation $$A\mathbf{x} = 0$$ .
(T/F) The solution set of $$A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$$ is obtained by translating the solution set of $$A\mathbf{x} = 0$$ .

Prove the second part of Theorem 6: Let $$\mathbf{w}$$ be any solution of $$A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$$ , and define $$\mathbf{v}_{h} = \mathbf{w} - \mathbf{p}$$ . Show that $$\mathbf{v}_{h}$$ is a solution of $$A\mathbf{x} = 0$$ . This shows that every solution of $$A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$$ has the form $$\mathbf{w} = \mathbf{p} + \mathbf{v}_{h}$$ , with $$\mathbf{p}$$ a particular solution of $$A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$$ and $$\mathbf{v}_{h}$$ a solution of $$A\mathbf{x} = 0$$ .
Suppose $$A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$$ has a solution. Explain why the solution is unique precisely when $$A\mathbf{x} = 0$$ has only the trivial solution.
Suppose $$A$$ is the $$3 \times 3$$ zero matrix (with all zero entries). Describe the solution set of the equation $$A\mathbf{x} = 0$$ .
If $$\mathbf{b} \neq 0$$ , can the solution set of $$A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$$ be a plane through the origin? Explain.
